comparison: Both strongly support the FUS experimental data and log-normal model (C4, C14, C24, C25, C39-C42, C45-C46, C48-C50). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative convergence of multiple analyses, while peer reviewers affirm the experimental evidence is 'solid' and 'very well done.' Peer result also includes C52 (uniform σ values), which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 supports C52 (uniform σ values) and C47 as key predictions of the scaling model. Peer R1 includes C52 in their overall affirmation of solid FUS experimental evidence but does not separately evaluate this specific prediction.

Both support the critical concentration estimates and methodology (C57-C62, C91, C94). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation and self-consistency checks. Peer reviewers accept the utility of the framework and do not challenge numerical estimates, though Reviewer 3 requests terminological clarification without disputing validity.

Both support the α-synuclein experimental data (C65-C70). OpenEval highlights quantitative exponents and consistency with scaling framework. Peer reviewers affirm the multi-protein experimental analysis is 'very well done' and particularly value the stationarity evidence (C70) as 'particularly valuable.'

Major disagreement on universality claims (C5, C15, C35, C75, C85). OpenEval supports approximate universality based on similar exponents across proteins. Peer Reviewer 1 expresses significant concerns, questioning whether observed exponents represent a new universality class or fit within existing percolation frameworks, stating 'the evidence supports the percolation+phase separation model rather than being close to a true critical point.'

Both support background claims about biomolecular condensates and empirical observations (C1-C2, C7-C10, C28-C29). OpenEval cites literature support, peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging these established contextual claims.

Disagreement on theoretical framing. OpenEval supports incompatibility with classical nucleation theory (C3, C11-C13) as well-established. Peer Reviewer 1 raises major concerns about theoretical interpretation, stating the work 'ignore[s]/miss[es] the connections to percolation' and finds 'connections between spinodal decomposition and second-order phase transitions are very confusing.'

Disagreement on theoretical framework. OpenEval supports the critical phenomena interpretation (C16-C21, C23) as consistent with standard theory. Peer Reviewer 1 challenges this framing, noting 'percolation theory...has clear-cut scaling laws that have essentially similar forms to the ansatz adopted by the authors and the commonalities/differences are not discussed.'

Disagreement on theoretical comparison. OpenEval supports the comparison with existing frameworks (C77-C84, C86-C87) as appropriate with fair identification of discrepancies. Peer Reviewer 1 finds the theoretical framing problematic, stating authors 'adopt a framing...to present a discovery of second-order features and connections to criticality - however they ignore/miss the connections to percolation.'

Partial overlap on model-independent approach (C22). OpenEval supports the scaling approach as reasonable inference from scale invariance. Peer Reviewer 1 questions the overall interpretation while acknowledging utility, creating uncertainty about whether the model-independent framing is appropriate.

Both support practical utility and future applications (C26-C27, C92-C93, C95-C96). OpenEval notes demonstrated utility with caveat about broader validation. Peer reviewers affirm the work is 'useful to the community' and 'provides a clear framework to help the community,' with editor noting it 'prompts further research.'

OpenEval rates biological and therapeutic implications (C97-C100) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative and require experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
Both support background literature claims (C1, C7-C9). OpenEval cites extensive literature support, peer reviewers implicitly accept these established contextual claims without challenge.

OpenEval supports methodological context and definitions (C31, C33, C72-C74, C76) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological definitions.

Both support experimental methods (C101-C107). OpenEval notes methods appear sound and reproducible with proper citations. Peer reviewers affirm 'the experimental analysis of distinct protein condensates is very well done,' implicitly validating the methodological approach.

OpenEval supports acknowledgment of open questions (C71, C88) as honest recognition of uncertainties. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about open questions in the field.

Peer Reviewer 3 specifically values the stationarity evidence (C30, C70) in Fig. 6 as 'particularly valuable' while suggesting improved presentation. OpenEval addresses C70 in R4 (α-synuclein) and C30 in R6 (background), but peer R6 focuses specifically on the temporal stability demonstration.
